title: Conjunctions
parentNote: Conjunctions are joining words! Think of them as glue that sticks two ideas together. Practice with daily life: "I want ice cream AND cake," "It is cold BUT sunny," "Do you want tea OR coffee?"
learnBullets: What a **conjunction** is — a word that joins words or sentences together
Making longer sentences by joining shorter ones
learnItFirst:
**What is a Conjunction?**
A conjunction is a **joining word**. It connects two words, phrases, or sentences together.

```
I like apples AND oranges. (joins two words)
She is tired BUT happy. (joins two ideas)
Do you want milk OR juice? (gives a choice)
```

**Common Conjunctions:**

| Conjunction | What it does | Example |
|-------------|--------------|---------|
| **and** | adds/joins similar things | I have a cat **and** a dog. |
| **but** | shows difference/contrast | She is small **but** strong. |
| **or** | gives a choice | Is it a boy **or** a girl? |
| **because** | gives a reason | I am happy **because** I won! |
| **so** | shows result | I was hungry, **so** I ate. |

**And vs But vs Or:**
- **AND** = Both things are true or wanted → I like pizza **and** pasta.
- **BUT** = One thing is different from expected → He is young **but** wise.
- **OR** = Only one of the things → Tea **or** coffee?

### 🧠 How to Choose the Right Conjunction
1. **Ask:** Am I adding things? → **and**
2. **Ask:** Am I showing something different/opposite? → **but**
3. **Ask:** Am I giving choices? → **or**
4. **Ask:** Am I giving a reason? → **because**
5. **Ask:** Am I showing what happened next? → **so**

questions.content: "I like apples ___ oranges."
questions.why: Adding two fruits together

questions.content: "Do you want tea ___ coffee?"
questions.why: Giving a choice between two drinks

questions.content: "She is tired ___ she cannot sleep."
questions.why: Contrast: tired → expected to sleep, but she can't

questions.content: "I ran fast ___ I was late."
questions.why: Giving the reason for running fast

questions.content: "The sun is shining ___ it is cold outside."
questions.why: Contrast: sunny but cold (opposite expectations)

questions.content: "Ravi ___ Priya are friends."
questions.why: Joining two names together

questions.content: "I was hungry, ___ I ate an apple."
questions.why: Result: hungry → so I ate

questions.content: "Is this your pen ___ pencil?"
questions.why: Asking which one — giving a choice

questions.content: "I fell down ___ I did not cry."
questions.why: Contrast: fell down but did not cry (unexpected)

questions.content: "She is happy ___ she got a gift."
questions.why: Giving the reason for being happy

questions.content: Which word is a conjunction?
questions.why: But is a conjunction (joining word)

questions.content: "I can read ___ write in English."
questions.why: Adding two abilities together

questions.content: Join the sentences: "She is young. She is very smart."

options.A: She is young and she is very smart.
options.B: She is young or she is very smart.
options.C: She is young so she is very smart.
options.D: She is young but she is very smart.

questions.why: Contrast: young but smart (unexpected)

questions.content: "We will go to the park ___ it does not rain."
questions.why: Condition: if it doesn't rain

questions.content: "The movie was long ___ interesting."
questions.why: Contrast: long but interesting

questions.content: "Do you play cricket ___ football?"
questions.why: Asking which sport — giving a choice

questions.content: "I closed the window ___ it was cold."
questions.why: Giving the reason for closing the window

questions.content: Join using "so": "It was raining. We stayed inside."

options.A: It was raining but we stayed inside.
options.B: It was raining so we stayed inside.
options.C: It was raining or we stayed inside.
options.D: It was raining and we stayed inside.

questions.why: Result: raining → so stayed inside

questions.content: "My father ___ mother both work."
questions.why: Joining father and mother

questions.content: "He studied hard ___ he passed the exam."
questions.why: Result: studied hard → so passed

questions.content: Which sentence uses "but" correctly?

options.A: I like ice cream but chocolate.
options.C: The bag is small but heavy.

questions.why: Correct contrast use

questions.content: "I want to play ___ I have homework."
questions.why: Contrast: want to play but have homework

questions.content: How many conjunctions are in this sentence? "I like mangoes and apples but not bananas or oranges."
questions.why: and, but, or = 3 conjunctions

questions.content: "She was sick, ___ she went to school."
questions.why: Contrast: sick but still went to school (unexpected)

questions.content: Join the sentences correctly: "Hurry up. You will be late."

options.A: Hurry up because you will be late.
options.B: Hurry up but you will be late.
options.C: Hurry up or you will be late.
options.D: Hurry up and you will be late.

questions.why: "Or" shows what will happen if you don't hurry

questions.content: Fill in both blanks: "I wanted to go outside ___ play ___ it was raining."
questions.why: Wanted to go and play, but it was raining

questions.content: Which sentence is INCORRECT?

options.B: Do you want rice and roti? (when giving a choice)
options.C: I am happy because I won.

questions.why: Should be "or" when giving a choice

questions.content: "My grandmother is old ___ very active. She walks ___ exercises every day ___ she stays healthy."
questions.why: Old BUT active, walks AND exercises, SO stays healthy

questions.content: Join using TWO conjunctions: "I was tired. I could not sleep. I drank warm milk."

options.A: I was tired but I could not sleep, so I drank warm milk.
options.B: I was tired or I could not sleep or I drank warm milk.
options.C: I was tired and I could not sleep and I drank warm milk.
options.D: I was tired because I could not sleep but I drank warm milk.

questions.why: Contrast + result

questions.content: Choose the correct conjunctions: "Study hard ___ you will fail. Work with friends ___ alone, ___ finish your project."
questions.why: Study or fail; friends or alone; but finish
